existing.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.
eligibility: Work experience in peace and development
Commitment to community and international service and the pursuit of peace
Not a spouse, lineal descendant, spouse of a lineal descendant, or parent or grandparent by blood of a living Rotary member in those categories
Not a former Rotary member, or a relative as described, within 36 months of that member's resignation
Rotaract club members who are not also Rotary club members are eligible to apply
Must wait three years between the end of a Rotary Peace Centers certificate or master's programme, or a Global Grant Scholarship, and the intended fellowship start date
existing.eligibility_summary: Dedicated leaders with work experience in peace and development who are committed to community and international service. Candidates must not be pursuing doctoral study, and are barred if they are a spouse, lineal descendant, or close blood relative of a current Rotary member, a former Rotary member within 36 months, or a recent Rotary Peace Fellow or Global Grant Scholarship recipient.
benefits: Up to 50 funded fellowships for master's degrees each year
Up to 120 funded fellowships for certificate studies each year
Access to eight Rotary Peace Centers worldwide
Global network of more than 1,900 alumni fellows working in over 140 countries
requirements: Submit an online application to The Rotary Foundation by 15 May
Demonstrate work experience in peace and development
Obtain a club or district recommendation where available
documents: Online application to The Rotary Foundation
Club or district recommendation, which is optional but supported
existing.english_requirement: All applications and recommendations must be submitted in English.
application_method: Apply online through The Rotary Foundation's Peace Fellowship application portal once the cycle opens
Ask a Rotary club or district to submit a recommendation as part of the application
Submit all materials in English by the 15 May global deadline
existing.selection_notes: Rotary members and clubs are central to recruiting candidates. Clubs and districts are not required to fund candidates. Applications are reviewed by Rotary Peace Centers staff and all qualified applications move forward for further consideration.
existing.best_fit: Experienced peace and development professionals and committed community leaders seeking a funded master's degree or professional development certificate at one of Rotary's partner peace centers.
existing.notes: Rotary awards up to 170 funded fellowships a year across eight peace centers. Since 2002 the program has trained more than 1,900 fellows who now work in over 140 countries, many in governments, NGOs, education and research institutions, peacekeeping and law enforcement agencies, and organizations such as the United Nations and the World Bank. Master's programmes last 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study. The certificate programme is a one-year blended learning option for working professionals who complete field studies and design and carry out a social change initiative. Rotary Peace Fellowships may not be used for doctoral study.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open in February and close 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications are submitted online to The Rotary Foundation and the global deadline is 15 May. The official application timeline states: "The 2027-28 Rotary Peace Fellowship application is now closed. The 2028-29 Rotary Peace Fellowship application will be available online in February 2027."
existing.program_type: Fully funded postgraduate fellowship in peace and development studies
